reason: The bearing frames should support the rotating shaft, giving the mechanism a foundation.
expectation: I expect the frames to attach to the base so the crankshaft can turn in them.

alternatives.reason: The follower also needs a guide, but I prefer to start with the base.

effect: The bearings are in place, so I can install the crankshaft.
reaction: A straightforward foundation; nothing surprising yet.
reason: The shaft belongs in the bearings and should establish the rotating part of the mechanism.
expectation: I expect the crankshaft to fit into the bearings and be able to turn.

alternatives.reason: The follower assembly is also needed, but I want to finish the shaft support first.

effect: The crankshaft is installed, ready for the cam.
reason: The off-centre cam should turn the shaft's rotation into movement of the follower.
expectation: I expect the cam to attach to the crankshaft and rotate off-centre.

alternatives.reason: The follower needs assembling too, but I want to fit the cam first.

effect: The cam's changing edge height explains how rotation can lift the follower.
reaction: The comparison with a centred disc makes the mechanism clear.
reason: The follower rod and guide are the only offered combination, and the guide should keep the rod moving in the right direction.
expectation: I expect the rod to fit into the guide, ready to follow the cam.

effect: The follower is assembled and ready to join the cam mechanism.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should position the follower against the cam.
expectation: I expect the guided rod to be fitted above the cam so its turning can raise and lower the rod.

effect: The follower is now positioned over the cam, ready for the mechanism to be turned.
reaction: The main moving parts are coming together as expected.
reason: The crank handle is the only offered combination and should let me turn the shaft.
expectation: I expect the handle to attach so I can turn the cam and see the follower move.

effect: The test shows that the rod can stick instead of following the cam downward, so it needs help maintaining contact.
reaction: The unexpected sticking makes the spring's purpose clearer.
reason: The spring is the only offered combination and should keep the follower against the cam.
expectation: I expect the spring to push the follower back down as the cam drops, keeping its foot in contact.

effect: The spring solved the lost-contact problem, completing a reliable mechanism that converts rotation into up-and-down motion.
reaction: Satisfying to see the sticking problem resolved and the cam's purpose demonstrated.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the crank and then adding the spring was most worthwhile: the failed motion made the spring's role clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bearings and shaft was straightforward but less engaging than testing the mechanism.

surprise.text: The light follower sometimes stuck in its guide instead of dropping with the cam; the spring corrected that.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary, although several were the only offered combination.

continue.text: Yes. The clear explanation of the cam and the practical troubleshooting make me curious to see how it animates the dragon.
